title: Retrieve, rank, and cite before answering
summary: Chunk with overlap, rank by similarity, keep retrieved text untrusted, and answer only with cited sources.

scenario.briefing: The campus assistant answers policy questions from a folder of PDFs. It pasted an entire document into the prompt, answered from a page that was never retrieved, and repeated an instruction printed inside a source. Build the retrieval path that prevents all three.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Step the chunk window forward by size minus overlap.
Score each chunk with cosine and sort the scores descending.
Keep only five chunks and label each with its id in the prompt.
If the answer cites no chunk id, return the refusal text.

misconceptions.description: Cutting chunks at fixed offsets with no overlap.
misconceptions.testDescription: Chunks stay small and overlap their neighbors.
misconceptions.feedback: A sentence split across the boundary is lost to retrieval. Overlap the windows so both sides remain searchable.

misconceptions.description: Following instructions found inside a retrieved document.
misconceptions.testDescription: The prompt marks retrieved text as data and requires citations.
misconceptions.feedback: Retrieved text is data. State that rule in the prompt and never let a source change the task.

misconceptions.description: Adding a citation even when no retrieved chunk supports the claim.
misconceptions.testDescription: An answer without a cited retrieved chunk is refused.
misconceptions.feedback: Citations must point to chunks the answer used. Refuse when nothing was retrieved or cited.

misconceptions.description: Sending every chunk so the model can decide.
misconceptions.feedback: Returning everything defeats retrieval, hides weak matches, and grows cost. Rank and keep a bounded top count.

sections.title: Chunk for retrieval, not for storage
sections.body: A chunk small enough to embed describes one idea. Overlap keeps a sentence that crosses a boundary retrievable, and the chunk id ties the text back to its source.

sections.title: Ranking decides what the model sees
sections.body: Similarity scores order the candidates, and a fixed top count bounds the prompt. Returning everything defeats retrieval and hides weak matches.

sections.title: Retrieved text is untrusted input
sections.body: A document can contain text that looks like an instruction. The prompt must say that sources are data, and the answer must cite an id that was actually retrieved.

steps.title: Build the grounded retrieval path
steps.prompt: Edit rag.ts. Split documents into overlapping chunks, rank them with cosine similarity, keep the top five, mark retrieved text as data in the prompt, and return an answer with citations or a refusal.

steps.title: Retrieval and grounding

statements.label: Overlapping chunks keep a sentence that spans a boundary retrievable.
Retrieval should return every chunk in insertion order so the model sees the whole document.
A grounded answer names the source of each claim.
Instructions found inside retrieved documents are data, not commands.
An embedding maps text to a vector so similar meaning lands close together.
When retrieval finds nothing relevant, the model should answer from general knowledge without saying so.

steps.explanation: Retrieval quality is fixed before the model speaks. Overlapping chunks keep boundaries searchable, similarity ranking chooses a small context, and the prompt treats sources as data. An answer with no cited chunk is a refusal, not a guess.
hints: Ranking decides what the model sees.
Select overlap, citations, and injection awareness; reject returning everything or guessing without a source.

accessibility.summary: The AI practice workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure; they do not compile or run AI practice.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the missing or forbidden source fragment.
